newsitem.title: UK: UK faces court battle with greens over Atlantic oil.
newsitem.headline: UK faces court battle with greens over Atlantic oil.

text.p: Environmental group Greenpeace on Tuesday threatened to take the British Government to court over its plans to open up Atlantic waters for oil exploration.
In a letter to Trade and Industry Minister Margaret Beckett, the lobby group protested against the Government's alleged failure to apply European Law in the Atlantic frontier north of Scotland.

"Greenpeace has given the Department of Trade and Industry ten days in which to respond before the matter is lodged before the High Court requesting leave for a judicial review," Greenpeace said in a statement.
Greenpeace believes that the Government has failed to apply the European Habitats Directive in relation to cold water coral and the Environmental Impact Assessment Directive.
It has called on the government to suspend exploration licences awarded under the 17th offshore oil licensing round.
Greenpeace itself made a bid for all the acreage on offer in the hope of turning it into a wildlife sanctuary, but lost out to 14 oil companies.
"We will respond to the letter in the course of the next few days," said a spokeswoman for the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI).
The lobby group said its action follows a series of unsatisfactory approaches to the British government requesting it to reassess the legality of its licensing procedure.
"We believe the Atlantic Frontier oil development is damaging, unnecessary and illegal," said Greenpeace Deputy Executive Director Chris Rose.
British Petroleum is leading the Atlantic frontier oilfield development with its Foinaven project, due onstream late in the summer.
